images.title: Swapping two digits
images.purpose: Show the number train of 3,925 before and after the digits 3 and 9 swap, with the new value of each swapped digit.
images.composition: Two number trains one above the other, joined by a swap symbol, with place letters and value tags under the coaches.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. Two number trains stacked, one in the upper half and one in the lower half. Each train, left to right: 1 small flat blue #0072B2 engine with no text, then 4 square coaches about 160 by 130 px joined by short couplers, each coach with 2 round wheels and one digit in large bold numerals (90 px). Above the upper train the number 3,925, above the lower train the number 9,325 (60 px bold dark). Upper train digits left to right: 3, 9, 2, 5. Lower train digits: 9, 3, 2, 5. In each train the first 2 coaches are reddish purple #CC79A7 with dark numerals and the last 2 coaches are blue #0072B2 with white numerals. Under each coach of each train a small place letter in dark text (36 px): Th, H, T, O. Under the first 2 coaches of each train a second small line, the value of that digit: upper train 3,000 and 900; lower train 9,000 and 300 (36 px, dark). Between the two trains, centred under coaches 1 and 2, 1 pair of curved amber #E69F00 arrows forming a swap symbol (one arrow from coach 1 to coach 2 and one back), and to the right of it the words swap 3 and 9 (44 px, dark).
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Swapping two different digits changes the number, because each digit takes the value of its new place.
images.description: Two number trains, 3,925 above and 9,325 below, with the first two coaches swapped by a pair of curved arrows and value tags 3,000 and 900 changing to 9,000 and 300.
images.context: Concept image for Swapping two digits changes the value. It follows the number train of coaches with two marked to swap, as the digit swap tool shows, and uses the video's own example, 3,925 to 9,325. Your maths book has no train picture; its digit swap questions use other numbers.
images.teaching_notes: Point at the 9: it was worth 900 and is now worth 9,000. The 3 was worth 3,000 and is now worth 300. The coloured coaches are the two that moved; the blue ones stay.

image_decisions.why: The number train before and after a swap shows each digit taking the value of its new place.
